title: Provision-to-ready automation sprint plan (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
content:
Doc owner: Vanessa Ortiz (Fleet automation)
PM/program: Talia Benson
Exec sponsors: Irene Choi (Infra), Priya Natarajan (Platform)
SRE lead: Rafael Mendes
Last updated: 2025-02-24

====

0) TL;DR
We’re doing a 4-week sprint to automate the Dedicated pool “provision-to-ready” lifecycle end-to-end (with safe manual overrides): infra provision -> image -> bootstrap -> validate -> mark Ready (and only then advertise to routing). Deliverables include a pipeline orchestrator path, versioned golden images, config validation gates (with audited break-glass), readiness gates including perf-canary, and a time-to-ready dashboard + alerts.

Success = we can pilot on 1–2 internal pools + one customer expansion with materially reduced and more predictable time-to-ready and fewer noisy handoffs.

Primary tracking: Linear project ENG-2741
Primary overview: Confluence “Provision-to-ready automation overview”

====

1) Goals / success metrics
Goals
- Reduce time-to-ready for new Dedicated GPU capacity by automating the full lifecycle and removing manual coordination.
- Improve predictability: stage budgets + “Ready” definition so Sales/CS can commit to shorter lead times.
- Reduce SRE/Infra toil: fewer ad-hoc steps, fewer “mystery stuck” handoffs, clearer rollback points.

Proposed success metrics (baseline in Week 1)
- Time-to-ready (TTR): p50/p95 for new pool bring-ups and expansions.
- Stage-level duration variance: stddev by stage should drop.
- Failure rate per stage: imaging/bootstrap/validation failures; retry counts.
- Operator toil: number of manual interventions per run; hours spent.

Target (draft; finalize after baseline)
- TTR p50: -40% vs baseline
- TTR p95: -30% vs baseline
- <= 1 manual intervention per provisioning run during pilot (excluding planned break-glass)

====

2) Scope (in-sprint)
In scope
- Fleet provisioning pipeline (operator-triggered): IaC apply + cluster bootstrap + control plane registration.
- Golden image hooks + rollout path (versioned/pinned; provenance checks).
- Config schema + validation + policy gates, including break-glass override (audited).
- Readiness gates: GPU health + networking/DNS/TLS + runtime smoke + perf-canary readiness suite.
- Observability: stage start/finish/failure events + TTR metrics + dashboard + alerts.
- Control plane Ready state transitions + routing consumption: only use Ready capacity.
- Runbooks + operator UX: minimal CLI hooks to trigger run and re-run stages safely.

Explicitly out of scope (reminder)
- Major redesign of serving runtime.
- Procurement/vendor contract changes.
- Full customer self-serve UI.

====

3) Workstreams + owners
Workstream A: Orchestration + state machine
- Owner: Gabe Wilson
- Review: Vanessa Ortiz, Ethan Park
- Tickets: ENG-2742 (state machine), ENG-2743 (TF wrapper), ENG-2750/2751 (CLI + manual override)
- Output: persisted state transitions, idempotent stage execution, pause/resume, stage re-run with caching

Workstream B: IaC + module standardization
- Owner: Nina Petrova
- Support: Keiko Yamamoto
- Tickets: ENG-2743 (TF orchestration), TF PRs via redwood-terraform
- Output: standardized module outputs consumed by orchestrator; regional defaults/guardrails; minimal SKU assumptions

Workstream C: Golden image + bootstrap hooks
- Owner: Sahana Iyer (CI/build) + Harish Reddy (ops execution)
- Security review: Marcus Lin
- Tickets: ENG-2744, plus runbook updates
- Output: versioned golden GPU node image, pinned driver/runtime prereqs, signing/provenance, rollback steps

Workstream D: Config schema + policy validation
- Owner: Benji Okafor
- Support: Jordan Lee
- Security: Kevin Osei
- Tickets: ENG-2745 (+ break-glass), ENG-2754 (drift detection)
- Output: schema, lint + policy checks, audited break-glass override, drift surfaced in control plane + dashboard

Workstream E: Readiness gates + perf-canary
- Owner: Rafael Mendes
- Support: Victor Alvarez (network checks), Rina Kobayashi (perf-canary)
- Tickets: ENG-2746 (gates), ENG-2747 (perf-canary)
- Output: deterministic pass/fail criteria; clear error messages; readiness suite benchmark with thresholding

Workstream F: Observability + dashboards + alerting
- Owner: Aisha Bello
- Support: Allison Grant, Sergio Costa, Logan Wright
- Tickets: ENG-2748/2749/2756
- Output: TTR metrics and stage breakdown; dashboard spec + implementation; alert policy (page vs ticket); backfill baseline

Workstream G: Docs + comms
- Owner: Kira Thompson
- Support: Connor O’Brien (release coordination)
- Tickets: runbooks + rollout checklist; CS/Sales messaging alignment via Lauren Bishop

====

4) Weekly milestones (what “done” looks like)
Week 1: Baseline + failure-mode inventory + design lock
- Collect baseline TTR from last ~10 Dedicated bring-ups/expansions (region/SKU split).
  - Owner: Jamal Pierce + Aisha Bello
  - Output: baseline doc + initial stage estimates + top delay causes
- Failure mode inventory: top 10 causes + where automation should add guardrails.
  - Owner: Rafael Mendes + Vanessa Ortiz
- Confirm definitions
  - “Provisioned” vs “Ready” semantics (control plane + routing)
  - Stage definitions and what constitutes stage completion
- Finalize ADRs / decisions
  - ADR-0142 orchestration model alignment
  - ADR-0143 config validation gates + break-glass
- Agree on stage budgets (draft) and an SLO proposal path

Week 2: Pipeline primitives shipped behind staging flag
- Orchestration primitives
  - State machine persisted + audit trail
  - Terraform wrapper with idempotency + retry semantics
  - Control plane endpoint to trigger run + query status
- Golden image build hook available + promotion path drafted
- Config schema v0 + validation library integrated in pipeline
- Emit structured stage events + correlation IDs (plumbed end-to-end)

Week 3: Readiness gates + Ready transitions + dashboards
- Readiness gates implemented
  - GPU health + ECC checks
  - Network/DNS/TLS checks
  - Runtime smoke test
- Perf-canary readiness suite integrated (minimal bench) as the final gating step before Ready
- Control plane Ready state transition implemented and consumed by routing
  - “Ready” is a hard gate for routing advertisement
- Initial dashboard + alert drafts (staging)
  - Stage breakdown + stuck-stage detection

Week 4: Pilot + docs + rollout readiness
- Pilot execution
  - 1–2 internal pools (staging + controlled prod-like) + 1 customer expansion window
- Iterate on failures
  - Fix top issues causing stuck stages, confusing errors, drift
- Runbooks
  - Provisioning runbook + image runbook + Ready troubleshooting guide updated
- Retro + follow-up backlog
  - What we shipped, what we didn’t, action items

====

5) Deliverables checklist (sprint exit criteria)
Automation
- [ ] Operator can trigger a provisioning run with CLI (dry-run supported)
- [ ] System provides stage-by-stage status + timestamps + correlation ID
- [ ] Manual override (pause/resume + break-glass for validation) is present and audited
- [ ] Stage re-run is safe (idempotent, no duplicate resources)

Readiness definition
- [ ] Control plane Ready state is only set after readiness gates + perf-canary pass
- [ ] Routing only uses capacity that is Ready

Observability
- [ ] Time-to-ready metric exists and can be broken down per stage
- [ ] Dashboard exists (filter by pool/customer/region/SKU)
- [ ] Alerts exist with ownership boundaries (page vs ticket)

Docs
- [ ] Runbooks are updated and linked from alerts
- [ ] Pilot rollout checklist exists with explicit rollback points

====

6) Risks / mitigations (living list)
Format: Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation | Owner | Notes

1) Multi-region + heterogeneous GPU SKUs cause brittle assumptions
- Likelihood: Medium
- Impact: High (pipeline fails on specific region/SKU)
- Mitigation: avoid SKU-specific hardcoding; define regional defaults + guardrails; add per-region config overrides validated via schema; include “known exceptions” allowlist with expiry
- Owner: Nina Petrova / Keiko Yamamoto
- Notes: imaging step historically flaky in at least one region due to artifact mirror latency

2) Config validation blocks legitimate edge cases (causes downtime / delays)
- Likelihood: High (early versions)
- Impact: High
- Mitigation: audited break-glass; staged enforcement (warn -> block); add migration/compat tools; maintain allowlist with review cadence
- Owner: Benji Okafor

3) Ready semantics inconsistent across control plane/routing/data plane
- Likelihood: Medium
- Impact: High (routing uses unvalidated capacity)
- Mitigation: explicit state machine; transactional “Ready set” only after perf-canary; add integration tests; add routing guard to ignore non-Ready states
- Owner: Ethan Park / Ravi Menon

4) Alerting too noisy (SRE page fatigue)
- Likelihood: Medium
- Impact: Medium/High
- Mitigation: paging only for stuck stages past p95 budget AND customer impact; otherwise auto-ticket; use burn-rate style thresholds for high failure rates
- Owner: Aisha Bello / Allison Grant

5) Secrets/IAM permissions and provenance aren’t ready (security blocks rollout)
- Likelihood: Medium
- Impact: High
- Mitigation: least privilege IAM review early (Week 2); signed artifacts for images/charts; document access model; security checklist required before prod flag
- Owner: Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei

6) Terraform apply is not reliably idempotent for expansions
- Likelihood: Medium
- Impact: High
- Mitigation: standardize module outputs; retries with backoff; explicit “no-op ok” behavior; detect quota/IAM failures and surface actionable errors
- Owner: Gabe Wilson / Nina Petrova

7) Perf-canary thresholds are too strict or too loose
- Likelihood: Medium
- Impact: Medium
- Mitigation: start with conservative thresholds; record metrics even on fail; allow override with audit for internal pilot only; adjust based on baseline runs
- Owner: Rina Kobayashi / Rafael Mendes

8) Operator UX unclear; increases toil vs reduces it
- Likelihood: Medium
- Impact: Medium
- Mitigation: CLI UX feedback loop; error messages must link to runbook sections; include “what to do next” per failure code
- Owner: Kira Thompson / Vanessa Ortiz

====

7) Dependencies / coordination points
- Control plane endpoint + authz for triggering provisioning runs (Platform)
- Terraform module refactors + standardized outputs (Infra)
- Helm chart pinning + bootstrap hooks (Serving runtime/platform deployment)
- Perf-canary readiness suite mode (Perf harness)
- Observability pack updates (dashboards/alerts templates)

Weekly syncs (proposal)
- Mon/Wed 30m “Provision-to-ready standup” (Infra + SRE + Platform)
- Fri 30m “Pilot readiness review” during Weeks 3–4

Slack channels
- #eng-infra (primary)
- #eng-sre (alerts/paging policy)
- #eng-platform (ready semantics)
- #architecture (ADRs)

====

8) Pilot plan (draft)
Internal pilot (staging)
- Choose 1 internal staging pool with representative region/SKU
- Run end-to-end at least 3 times (including one stage re-run and one intentional failure injection)
- Success criteria
  - end-to-end completes without manual intervention (except allowed break-glass test)
  - dashboard shows complete stage trace

Customer pilot expansion
- Pick 1 customer expansion window w/ CS aligned on comms + rollback
- Keep pool out of routing until Ready
- On-call coverage
  - Infra on-point: Harish Reddy
  - SRE on-point: Miles Thornton
  - Platform on-point: Ravi Menon

Rollback plan (high-level)
- Feature-flagged: ability to fall back to current manual/legacy steps
- If validation/perf-canary is flaky: disable gating but keep metrics (internal only) -> do not do this for customer pilot without Irene+Rafael approval
- If routing misbehaves: hard stop advertising new pool IDs except via explicit allowlist

====

9) Open questions (need answers this week)
- What is the exact Ready definition for expansions vs new pools?
  - Is “Ready” set per-node or per-pool? (We need per-pool for routing, but nodes can fail health.)
- What are our initial stage budgets (draft table) and what are acceptable exceptions?
- Break-glass policy
  - who can invoke (admin list)?
  - what logging/audit is required?
  - do we require a follow-up ticket automatically?
- Perf-canary
  - which model(s) for the readiness suite? do we need per-SKU expectations?
  - do we store raw results and where?

====

10) Notes to self / scratch
- Don’t underestimate “imaging” variability. We need detection + fallback path (mirror/prewarm).
- Make sure correlation ID is consistent across: provisioning service -> TF -> helm/bootstrap -> perf-canary -> control plane state transition -> dashboards.
- For alerting, default should be ticket creation + Slack notification; pages only when customer timeline is at risk.

====
